example.title: Decision Framework
example.code:
✅ AI Engineering is for you if:
  • You like building products, not writing papers
  • You're fine with non-deterministic systems
  • You enjoy reading model docs and changelogs weekly
  • You want $150K–$500K comp without a PhD
  • You like shipping things real users touch

❌ Consider other roles if:
  • You want to invent new models → Research Scientist
  • You want to train from scratch → ML Engineer
  • You want to analyze data → Data Scientist
  • You want stable, deterministic systems → SWE / DE

📊 Your first test: ship the Phase 1 CLI assistant.
   If you enjoy the loop, you're on the right track.

example.title: Your First LLM Call — CLI Career Advisor
example.code:
# Phase 1: ship a CLI assistant in 30 lines
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

def career_advisor(question: str) -> str:
    """v0.1 — naive single-shot career advisor."""
    msg = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",
        max_tokens=512,
        system="You are a senior FAANG hiring manager. "
               "Be direct, terse, and brutally honest.",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}],
    )
    return msg.content[0].text

if __name__ == "__main__":
    q = input("Career question: ")
    print(career_advisor(q))

# $ python advisor.py
# > "I'm a DE with 4 yrs. Aim for Senior AI Eng at Anthropic?"
#
# > Yes — but reposition. Your DE work IS AI-adjacent.
#   Frame: 'shipped data systems that powered ML at scale.'
#   Build one RAG project. Apply in 6 weeks.

# Cost: $0.003 per call. Latency: 1.2s. You just shipped.

lesson.overview: Python is non-negotiable. You need enough to build CLI tools, FastAPI endpoints, async streams, and orchestrate LLM calls. You do NOT need numpy/torch wizardry.

example.title: Structured LLM Output with Pydantic
example.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Literal
import anthropic, json

class CareerVerdict(BaseModel):
    fit_score: int        # 0-100
    rec: Literal["apply", "skip", "reposition"]
    reasons: list[str]
    next_action: str

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

def assess(resume: str, job: str) -> CareerVerdict:
    msg = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",
        max_tokens=512,
        system="Return ONLY valid JSON matching the schema.",
        messages=[{
            "role": "user",
            "content": f"Resume:\n{resume}\n\nJob:\n{job}\n\n"
                       f"Return JSON with: fit_score (0-100), "
                       f"rec, reasons[], next_action."
        }],
    )
    raw = msg.content[0].text
    return CareerVerdict(**json.loads(raw))

# verdict.fit_score → 78
# verdict.rec       → "apply"
# Type-safe AI output. This is the AI Engineer pattern.

example.title: 3-Step Pipeline — Resume → Skills → Job Match
example.code:
# Step 1: extract structured skills from resume
skills = llm(SYSTEM_EXTRACT, user=resume_text)
# → {"languages": ["Python","SQL"], "years": 4, ...}

# Step 2: critique the extraction (catch hallucinations)
critique = llm(SYSTEM_CRITIQUE,
    user=f"Resume:\n{resume_text}\n\nExtracted:\n{skills}")
if critique["confidence"] < 0.8:
    skills = llm(SYSTEM_EXTRACT_V2, user=resume_text)

# Step 3: match to job requirements
verdict = llm(SYSTEM_MATCH,
    user=f"Skills:\n{skills}\n\nJob:\n{job_text}")

# Each step is independently testable.
# Each step can be evaluated. Each step can be cached.
# This is what 'AI Engineering' actually looks like.

lesson.overview: Embeddings turn text into vectors. Vector DBs let you search by meaning instead of keywords. This is the foundation of every RAG system.

example.title: Embed & Index 10K Job Descriptions
example.code:
from openai import OpenAI
import psycopg2
client = OpenAI()

def embed(text: str) -> list[float]:
    return client.embeddings.create(
        model="text-embedding-3-small",
        input=text,
    ).data[0].embedding

# 1. Create pgvector table
conn.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE jobs (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        title TEXT,
        company TEXT,
        description TEXT,
        embedding VECTOR(1536)
    );
    CREATE INDEX ON jobs USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
""")

# 2. Embed and store 10K jobs
for job in jobs:
    vec = embed(f"{job.title} at {job.company}\n{job.description}")
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO jobs (title, company, description, embedding) "
        "VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)",
        (job.title, job.company, job.description, vec),
    )

# 3. Semantic search
query_vec = embed("Senior AI Eng remote, RAG experience")
results = conn.execute("""
    SELECT title, company, 1 - (embedding <=> %s) AS similarity
    FROM jobs
    ORDER BY embedding <=> %s
    LIMIT 10
""", (query_vec, query_vec)).fetchall()

lesson.overview: RAG = Retrieval Augmented Generation. Give the model your data without retraining it. The #1 most-asked-for AI feature at every company.

linkCheck.youtubeTitle: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models | Andrej Karpathy

lesson.overview: Vanilla embedding search misses 30% of relevant docs. Hybrid (BM25 + embedding) plus a cross-encoder re-ranker is the production-grade pattern.

example.title: Hybrid Search + Re-rank for Jobs
example.code:
import cohere
co = cohere.Client()

# 1. Get top-50 by hybrid (BM25 + embedding) — fast & broad
candidates = hybrid_search(query="Senior AI Eng RAG remote",
                           k=50)

# 2. Re-rank top-50 → top-5 with cross-encoder — slow but precise
reranked = co.rerank(
    model="rerank-3.5",
    query="Senior AI Eng RAG remote",
    documents=[c.description for c in candidates],
    top_n=5,
)

best_jobs = [candidates[r.index] for r in reranked.results]

# Recall@5 jumped from 0.62 → 0.91. Same data, better retrieval.

example.title: Career Advisor Agent — 3 Real Tools
example.code:
tools = [
    {"name": "search_jobs",        # → vector search
     "description": "Find relevant jobs for the user.",
     "input_schema": {...}},
    {"name": "salary_lookup",      # → levels.fyi API
     "description": "Get total comp for role/level/loc.",
     "input_schema": {...}},
    {"name": "schedule_mock",      # → calendar API
     "description": "Book a mock interview slot.",
     "input_schema": {...}},
]

def run_agent(user_msg: str):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": user_msg}]
    while True:
        resp = client.messages.create(
            model="claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",
            tools=tools, max_tokens=2048, messages=messages,
        )
        if resp.stop_reason == "end_turn":
            return resp.content[0].text
        # Otherwise: model called a tool
        for block in resp.content:
            if block.type == "tool_use":
                result = TOOL_FN[block.name](**block.input)
                messages.append({"role": "assistant",
                                 "content": resp.content})
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [{
                    "type": "tool_result",
                    "tool_use_id": block.id,
                    "content": str(result),
                }]})

lesson.overview: Real agents loop: plan → act → observe → re-plan. Memory matters. Most multi-agent setups fail — single agent with great tools usually wins.

linkCheck.youtubeTitle: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models | Andrej Karpathy

lesson.overview: When one agent isn't enough: orchestrator + workers, parallel sub-agents, hierarchical teams. Use sparingly — costs and failure modes compound fast.

example.title: Orchestrator + 3 Worker Agents (Career Advisor)
example.code:
# ORCHESTRATOR receives the user query and dispatches.
def orchestrator(user_query: str):
    plan = llm(SYSTEM_PLAN, user=user_query)
    # plan = ["resume_analyzer", "job_finder", "interview_coach"]

    results = parallel_map({
        "resume_analyzer": lambda: agent_resume(user_query),
        "job_finder":      lambda: agent_jobs(user_query),
        "interview_coach": lambda: agent_interview(user_query),
    })

    return llm(SYSTEM_SYNTHESIZE,
        user=f"Synthesize into one career plan:\n{results}")

# Each worker has its OWN tools, OWN system prompt, OWN model.
# Resume analyzer → cheap fast model.
# Interview coach → big slow model.
# Run in parallel → 3× faster than sequential.

example.title: Eval Suite — Catch Regressions Before Prod
example.code:
# golden.jsonl — 100 hand-labeled (input, expected) pairs
GOLDEN = [
    {"input": "DE 4yrs Stripe → Senior AI Eng Anthropic?",
     "expected_rec": "apply",
     "expected_keywords": ["RAG", "rebrand", "DE-to-AI"]},
    # ... 99 more
]

def eval_advisor(prompt_version: str) -> dict:
    pass_count = 0
    for ex in GOLDEN:
        out = career_advisor(ex["input"], prompt=prompt_version)

        # Code-based check
        if out["rec"] != ex["expected_rec"]: continue

        # LLM-as-judge for nuance
        judge = llm(JUDGE_SYSTEM,
            user=f"Q: {ex['input']}\nA: {out['text']}\n"
                 f"Must mention: {ex['expected_keywords']}\n"
                 f"Score 0-1.")
        if judge["score"] >= 0.8: pass_count += 1

    return {"pass_rate": pass_count / len(GOLDEN)}

# v1 prompt: 0.62
# v2 prompt: 0.81
# v3 prompt: 0.79  ← regression caught BEFORE prod

lesson.overview: Production AI needs input validation, output filtering, PII redaction, and refusal handling. One bad output can land you in the news.

phases.title: Ship It For Real
phases.description: Streaming APIs, deployment, prompt caching, model routing, prompt versioning, rollbacks. The bar is 'works for 1000 users at 3am'.

lesson.overview: Wrap your model in an API, stream responses to a UI, deploy to a serverless platform. The bar isn't 'works on localhost' — it's 'works for 1000 users at 3am'.

example.title: Streaming Career Advisor — FastAPI
example.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import anthropic

app = FastAPI()
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

@app.post("/advise")
async def advise(req: AdviseRequest):
    async def stream():
        with client.messages.stream(
            model="claude-3-5-sonnet-latest",
            max_tokens=1024,
            system=ADVISOR_SYSTEM,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": req.question}],
        ) as s:
            for text in s.text_stream:
                yield f"data: {text}\n\n"
            yield "data: [DONE]\n\n"

    return StreamingResponse(stream(), media_type="text/event-stream")

# Deploy: 'vercel deploy' or 'fly launch'.
# 100ms TTFB, streams char-by-char to your React frontend.
# This is a real product. Recruiters can click the URL.

lesson.overview: Token costs add up fast. Caching, prompt compression, model routing, and batching can cut costs 10× without sacrificing quality.
